Sam, Marissa —

Attached are the artifacts per Marissa's note. Short summary of what's included and what we redacted:

1) redwood_kms_rotation_manifest_2027-07-sample.csv (attached) — anonymized sample of three rotation events for a tenant-like tag. Columns: event_id, utc_timestamp, tenant_tag, old_key_fingerprint, new_key_fingerprint, actor_id, rotation_trigger (scheduled/manual/compromise), verification_checksum. We removed PII and replaced tenant IDs with stable pseudo-tags (e.g., tenant-A-xyz).

2) helios_sig_wrap_flow_diagram.png (attached) — a simple swimlane showing: DEK generation (per-request), DEK encrypted under KEK (either customer-provided HSM KEK or Redwood KEK), wrapped_key stored in tenant metadata, automatic re-wrapping during key rotation, and cross-region replication of wrapped blobs with readonly replication keys.

3) sig-supplement-byok-dek-annotations.pdf (attached) — short Q&A:
   - BYOK: KEKs stored in customer CloudHSM are non-exportable; Redwood performs KMS calls to wrap/unwrap but never holds KEK material.
   - Redwood-managed KEK: protected in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM pool (CloudHSM / HSM appliance depending on deployment); KEKs are rotation-friendly and have signing attestation available.
   - Rotation cadence: default 90 days for KEK rotation; DEKs are ephemeral and rotated per-versioning policies or when tenant requests immediate rewrap. Automated safety checks validate checksum + signature before completing rollover.

Notes on auditability: rotation events are signed with a platform key and stored in an append-only ledger (hash chain) — we can provide log excerpts under NDA for complete samples.

If Helios needs the raw signed ledger excerpt (including signature verification step), let us know and we'll route through security team for an NDA and MSA amendment.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security — Redwood Inference
